RBA Governor Michele Bullock told a parliamentary committee that upside inflation risks flagged in August are now materialising, driven by Middle East oil prices, the AI boom and extreme weather, even as growth slows and jobless holds at 4.5%.

Bullock's acknowledgment that upside inflation risks flagged in August are now materialising, rather than merely a possibility, leans hawkish ahead of the Board's meeting in just over a week. Her explicit link between Middle East oil price gains and both direct and indirect inflation pass-through gives markets a clearer read on why a further hike remains live, even as she flagged that Australian growth is slowing. The Australian dollar could find some support from the hawkish tone, particularly the reference to other advanced-economy central banks also responding to the same global inflation shock, though the acknowledgment of softening housing and gradually easing labour market conditions tempers how far that repricing is likely to run. Overall, the testimony reads as consistent with, rather than a clear upgrade to, the roughly 70 to 75% probability already priced for a hike at the 28-29 September meeting.

This is all from Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Bullock's prepared statement. There will be Q&A to follow soon.

She said upside inflation risks flagged in the August Statement on Monetary Policy are now materialising, citing the Middle East conflict, the AI boom and extreme weather as pushing up energy, agricultural and technology-related prices

Oil prices have risen sharply again, adding directly to inflation through petrol prices and indirectly as firms pass on higher input costs, a dynamic Bullock said other advanced-economy central banks are also responding to

The unemployment rate stood at 4.5%, with labour market conditions close to, but a little tighter than, full employment, and the employment-to-population ratio near a record high

Bullock said domestic demand growth is easing as expected, with the full effect of this year's 75 basis points of rate increases yet to be felt, while business investment has picked up strongly on data centre and renewable energy spending

She reiterated that the Board's task is to determine whether the tightening delivered so far will be enough to return inflation to target in a reasonable time, with the next meeting due in just over a week

Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock told the House of Representatives Standing Committee on Economics on Thursday that inflation has remained above target since picking up in the second half of 2025, with both headline and underlying measures running around or a little above 3.5% over the past year. Bullock said the increase partly reflects capacity pressures in the domestic economy, compounded by the conflict in the Middle East, which has lifted inflation directly through petrol prices and indirectly as firms pass higher input costs through to other goods and services. "Inflation is too high," she told the committee, adding that the Board is focused on ensuring it does not become embedded in price and wage-setting behaviour.

On the labour market, Bullock said conditions remain close to, but a little tighter than, full employment. The unemployment rate stood at 4.5%, low by historical standards, and the share of the population with a job is close to a record high.

Turning to the outlook, Bullock said the RBA's August Statement on Monetary Policy had assessed the risks to its inflation forecast, which had inflation returning to around the midpoint of the target band only by late 2027, as skewed to the upside. She said developments since then suggest some of those upside risks are now materialising. Global cost pressures have increased, with the Middle East conflict, the AI boom and extreme weather events adding upward pressure on energy, agricultural and technology-related prices. Oil and related prices have risen sharply again, and the Bank's business liaison program is picking up widespread reports of firms passing on higher costs, a trend Bullock said needs to remain contained rather than becoming embedded in ongoing price and wage decisions. She noted that central banks in several other advanced economies are responding to the same global inflation shock by raising rates or signalling they may need to.

On domestic activity, Bullock said demand growth has eased in the first half of 2026 broadly as expected, with the full effect of this year's cumulative 75 basis points of rate increases yet to flow through given the usual lags in monetary policy. The impact of the Middle East conflict on activity has been relatively modest so far despite weaker confidence, with household spending growth moderating gradually while business investment has picked up strongly, driven largely by data centre and renewable energy spending. Bullock said continued weak productivity growth means the economy cannot grow strongly without adding to inflation pressure, calling it a fundamental challenge for the years ahead. She said the Monetary Policy Board's meeting in just over a week's time will assess whether the tightening delivered so far will be sufficient to return inflation to target within a reasonable timeframe.

UBS's view that further hikes remain likely this year points to continued support for the US dollar and real yields, a combination that raises the opportunity cost of holding gold and could see some of August's ETF inflows unwind in the near term. Longer term, the bank argues gold's investment case remains intact, underpinned by rising global debt, an expected weaker dollar and the prospect of rate cuts next year.

Other analysts framed the unanimous vote as evidence the Fed is taking a firmer stance against persistent inflation, much of it tied to elevated energy prices flowing from the conflict in the Middle East, with a further hike by year end widely seen as close to settled. Beyond that, views diverge sharply on how long above-target inflation could persist, with one long-term assessment suggesting price stability might not return for years given structural pressures from energy security, fiscal spending and the capital intensity of the AI investment cycle.

The Federal Reserve raised its target interest rate range by 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4.0% on Wednesday, in a decision made under new Chair Kevin Warsh and passed unanimously by the rate-setting committee for the first time in more than three years. Sticky inflation, with rising energy prices a significant contributor, was central to the central bank's reasoning.

UBS Global Wealth Management said the Fed's updated projections show most policymakers expect at least one further hike this year, a backdrop it believes could keep US real yields and the dollar elevated and raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, adding to near-term volatility for the metal. The bank noted gold exchange traded funds drew solid inflows in August amid concerns over Fed independence and rising debt levels, and said some of those holdings could reverse following what it called a hawkish hike. Even so, UBS argued the decision and the prospect of further tightening are already widely anticipated by markets and do not undermine gold's longer-term investment case, pointing to rising global debt, an expected weaker dollar over time and likely Fed rate cuts next year as supportive factors, alongside elevated geopolitical uncertainty.

Other analysts characterised the unanimous vote as a sign the Fed has found firmer footing after a long stretch of caution, arguing the committee prioritised concerns about inflation's drag on business decision making over arguments for standing pat. One long-term assessment suggested that if the Fed's own forecasts prove accurate, the US could see roughly eight years of above-target inflation before price stability is restored, tying that outlook to structural shifts including geopolitical fragmentation, energy security concerns, larger government spending, supply-chain duplication and the capital intensity of the AI investment boom. That analyst noted Warsh's press conference struck a similarly hawkish tone, with the new chair suggesting rates remain below neutral even after the increase, and said further tightening stays on the table unless resilient activity and elevated capital spending both ease.

Other commentary was more measured, framing the hike as a straightforward call given inflation has sat above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years alongside a fully employed labour market, while cautioning that the outlook beyond this year is murkier given ongoing geopolitical and energy uncertainty out of the Persian Gulf. Several analysts also pointed to the position this places Warsh in personally, since he was brought into the role expected to deliver the rate cuts favoured by President Trump, yet his first significant decision was an increase, a dynamic some said could echo the friction Trump previously showed toward former Chair Jerome Powell. Those analysts said the Fed will likely want to see a sustained easing in Middle East tensions before looking past the current inflation spike, and that Warsh's stated commitment to further work on inflation will eventually need to be matched with clarity on how long that work will take.

Federal Reserve Chair Warsh

Le point de vue d'UBS selon lequel de nouvelles hausses restent probables cette année indique un soutien continu du dollar américain et des rendements réels, une combinaison qui augmente le coût d'opportunité de la détention d'or et pourrait voir une partie des entrées d'ETF d'août se résorber à court terme. L'inflation fixe, la hausse des prix de l'énergie étant un facteur important, a été au cœur du raisonnement de la banque centrale.

UBS Global Wealth Management a déclaré que les projections actualisées de la Fed montrent que la plupart des décideurs s'attendent à au moins une nouvelle hausse cette année, une toile de fond qui, selon elle, pourrait maintenir les rendements réels américains et le dollar élevés et augmenter le coût d'opportunité de la détention d'or, ajoutant à la volatilité à court terme pour le métal.La banque a noté que les fonds négociés en bourse de l'or avaient attiré de solides entrées en août au milieu des inquiétudes concernant l'indépendance de la Fed et la hausse des niveaux d'endettement, et a déclaré que certaines de ces positions pourraient s'inverser à la suite de ce qu'elle a appelé une hausse belliciste.Malgré cela, UBS a fait valoir que la décision et la perspective d'un nouveau resserrement sont déjà largement anticipées par les marchés et ne minent pas les arguments d'investissement à long terme de l'or, soulignant la hausse de la dette mondiale, un dollar plus faible attendu au fil du temps et des réductions probables des taux de la Fed l'année prochaine comme facteurs favorables, parallèlement à une incertitude géopolitique élevée.

D'autres analystes ont qualifié le vote unanime de signe que la Fed a trouvé une base plus solide après une longue période de prudence, arguant que le comité accordait la priorité aux préoccupations concernant la traînée de l'inflation sur la prise de décision des entreprises plutôt qu'aux arguments en faveur d'un statu quo.Une évaluation à long terme a suggéré que si les propres prévisions de la Fed s'avéraient exactes, les États-Unis pourraient connaître environ huit ans d'inflation supérieure à la cible avant que la stabilité des prix ne soit rétablie, liant ces perspectives à des changements structurels, notamment la fragmentation géopolitique, les préoccupations en matière de sécurité énergétique, les dépenses publiques plus importantes, la duplication de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et l'intensité capitalistique du boom de l'investissement dans l'IA.Cet analyste a noté que la conférence de presse de Warsh avait eu un ton tout aussi belliciste, le nouveau président suggérant que les taux restent inférieurs à la neutralité même après l'augmentation, et a déclaré qu'un resserrement supplémentaire restait sur la table à moins que l'activité résiliente et les dépenses en capital élevées ne se relâchent.

Today's appearance is a routine parliamentary hearing rather than a policy decision, so the direct market impact should be limited unless Bullock's answers shift the tone from recent RBA communication. Even so, any fresh comment on inflation persistence or the labour market could move rate pricing ahead of the September 28-29 meeting, where a further 25 basis point increase is currently priced at around 70 to 75%.

The Australian dollar and short end yields are the most likely to react to any hawkish or dovish surprise in the Q&A, given how closely positioned markets already are for a hike. With trimmed mean inflation still running above the RBA's 2 to 3% target band, traders will be listening for any signal on how much more tightening the board thinks is needed.

Bullock fronts parliament today with a live rate call still hanging on next month's meeting.

Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock appears before the House of Representatives Standing Committee on Economics today, accompanied by Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser, Assistant Governor (Economic) Sarah Hunter and Assistant Governor (Financial System) Brad Jones. The appearance is a routine parliamentary hearing at which the Governor updates the committee on the Bank's operations before taking questions, rather than a scheduled monetary policy speech, but the timing puts it firmly on the radar of currency and rates traders.

The RBA is in the midst of a rate hiking cycle that resumed early this year. The board lifted the cash rate by 25 basis points at each of its first three meetings of 2026, on 3 February, 17 March and 5 May, taking it to 4.35%. It has since held twice, at its 6 June and 11 August meetings, judging that the earlier increases needed time to work through the economy. At the August meeting the board kept policy on hold unanimously, noting that financial conditions had tightened following the three earlier hikes and that the economy appeared to be slowing broadly as expected.

Inflation remains the key swing factor. The RBA's preferred trimmed mean measure, which strips out the most volatile price moves, was running at 3.6% year on year as of the July data, unchanged from the prior reading and still above the top of the bank's 2% to 3% target band. Headline CPI eased to 3.5% over the same period. That combination, cooling headline inflation alongside sticky underlying price pressure, is the backdrop against which markets are pricing today's testimony and next month's decision.

The board's next scheduled meeting falls on 28-29 September, and a further 25 basis point increase is currently priced at around 70% to 75%, reflecting a market view that the inflation fight is not yet over even as the economy shows signs of slowing. Today's committee hearing gives Bullock and her colleagues a chance to address that pricing directly through questions from MPs, though any market reaction is likely to hinge on unscripted responses rather than a prepared statement.

There's also a running, mostly quietly spoken tension between the RBA and the government over spending's role in inflation. Bullock has acknowledged in past parliamentary hearings that public demand feeds into the same aggregate demand pressures the Bank is trying to cool, telling one committee plainly that it doesn't take much additional spending to make the job of returning inflation to target more challenging. Treasurer Jim Chalmers has pushed back on any suggestion the government is the main culprit, pointing instead to private demand and global factors such as elevated energy prices. Neither side tends to press the point too hard in public, and today's hearing is unlikely to change that, but the underlying friction over how much fiscal policy is complicating the RBA's task remains part of the backdrop to any further hike.

Australian Treasurer Chalmers

Aucune des deux parties n'a tendance à insister trop fort en public, et l'audience d'aujourd' hui ne devrait pas changer cela, mais la friction sous-jacente sur la mesure dans laquelle la politique budgétaire complique la tâche de la RBA reste une partie de la toile de fond de toute nouvelle hausse.

Trésorier australien Chalmers

The Bank of Japan is expected to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% today, its highest since 1993, with markets focused less on the hike itself than on Governor Ueda's guidance on the pace of further tightening.

With a quarter point hike now close to fully priced, the tradeable content today sits less in the decision itself and more in Governor Ueda's guidance on what follows it. USD/JPY has already fallen from around 160 to near 153 over recent weeks as hike odds built, which leaves room for a "buy the rumour, sell the fact" reaction if Ueda's tone stays cautious and data dependent.Goldman Sachsargues a faster tightening path would put upward pressure on Japanese government bond yields and could support the yen further by narrowing the policy gap with other major central banks, though the read-through for the Nikkei is more mixed, since a firmer yen tends to weigh on exporter earnings even as higher rates pressure valuations elsewhere.Reuters-polled economistssee the policy rate reaching 1.5% by the end of March next year and 1.75% by mid-2027, so today's move is being treated as one step in a longer path rather than the end of the story.

A BoJ hike looks like a formality today; the real fight is over how fast rates rise from here.

The rate statement has no fixed release time; expect it in a roughly 0230 to 0330 GMT window, with Ueda's press conference set for 0630 GMT (0230 US Eastern)

A larger 50 basis point move has been played down, with board member Kazuyuki Masu saying inflation is nearing target without a sharp overshoot

Goldman Sachs calls the hike a done deal and flags growing odds of a faster pace, potentially with another move in December, plus room for JGB yields to climb further

Reuters-polled economists see the policy rate at 1.5% by end March 2027 and 1.75% by the second quarter of 2027

The Bank of Japan wraps up a two day policy meeting today, and a rate hike is being treated by markets and economists as close to a formality. A quarter point increase to 1.25% would take the policy rate to its highest level since 1993 and mark the central bank's sixth increase since it exited ultra loose policy in 2024. Unlike some other major central banks, the BoJ does not fix a firm release time for its statement, so a window of roughly 0230 to 0330 GMT is the best estimate. Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference follows at a scheduled 0630 GMT.

With the hike itself largely priced in, the more interesting question for markets is what the BoJ signals about the pace of tightening from here. Reuters reporting, citing people familiar with the central bank's thinking, suggests the board has no preset view on a terminal rate and remains split between hawks who believe underlying inflation is already close to the 2% target and more cautious members such as Toichiro Asada, who dissented against June's increase. Ueda is expected to avoid committing to a specific timetable, though he may repeat earlier comments suggesting the bank could move faster if financial conditions are judged too loose. A larger, 50 basis point move has been played down given the absence of any sharp overshoot in wage or price data, a view echoed publicly by board member Kazuyuki Masu.

Goldman Sachs frames today's decision as effectively settled and argues there is a growing case for a quicker pace, with scope for a further move as soon as December. The bank points to elevated energy prices, strong AI related demand, a weaker yen and what it sees as still accommodative fiscal policy under Prime Minister Takaichi as forces that could push inflation higher than currently expected. Goldman's central call is for further gains in Japanese government bond yields, arguing current levels look too low against a resilient domestic economy, though it also flags the read-through for the yen and Nikkei from any shift to a faster hiking path.

The yen's recent strength adds another layer to today's setup. USD/JPY has fallen from around 160 to near 153 over the past several weeks (currently straddling 156.00)  as rate hike expectations built, leaving open the possibility of a "buy the rumour, sell the fact" reaction if Ueda sticks to a cautious, data dependent tone. Reuters-polled economists expect the policy rate to reach 1.5% by the end of March next year and 1.75% by the second quarter of 2027, with most seeing the terminal rate at least that high.

Bank of Japan Governor Ueda presser due at 0630 GMT / 0230 US Eastern time on Friday, September 18, 2026.

Japan releases August national CPI today, with economists expecting core inflation to hold at 1.8% year on year, still below the BoJ's 2% target, as the central bank meets to decide on a widely expected 25 basis point rate hike to 1.25%.

Japan's inflation data typically carries limited standalone weight on the yen and JGB yields when a Bank of Japan decision lands the same day, and today looks no different. Traders are more focused on the outcome of the BoJ meeting and Governor Ueda's press conference this afternoon than on the CPI print itself, given a rate hike is already close to fully priced by swap markets. A core reading in line with the 1.8% consensus would likely do little to alter that path, while a surprise miss or beat could still nudge USD/JPY and short-dated JGB yields in the hours before the policy announcement. Some analysts have also flagged the chance of yen intervention chatter resurfacing around the thin Silver Week holiday trading conditions that follow the meeting.

Japan's August CPI lands as the BoJ prepares to lift rates to a 31-year high, with the inflation print unlikely to move the needle either way.

Japan is due to release national CPI data for August today; the Tokyo reading, seen three weeks ago, showed core inflation (ex fresh food) at 1.8% year on year, up from 1.7% in July and in line with forecasts

Economists polled by Reuters expect national core CPI to also hold at 1.8% for August, level with July and still short of the BoJ's 2% target

Producer price inflation accelerated to roughly a three-and-a-half-year high in August, a sign of building upstream cost pressure

The BoJ concludes a two-day policy meeting today, with swap markets pricing a near-certain 25 basis point hike to 1.25%, which would be the highest level since 1993

Today's CPI print is expected to be read as confirmation of the broader trend rather than a deciding factor for the board

Governor Ueda holds a press conference this afternoon; a fuller BoJ preview will follow separately

Japan is due to publish its national consumer price index for August today, a release that will draw less attention than usual given the Bank of Japan's own policy decision lands on the same day. TheTokyo area figures, seen as a leading indicator for the national number, already gave traders an early read three weeks ago: core CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.8% year on year in August, up slightly from 1.7% in July and in line with the median forecast. A closely watched gauge that strips out both fresh food and energy also edged higher, moving closer to the BoJ's 2% inflation target.

Economists polled by Reuters expect the national figure to track that pattern, with core CPI forecast to hold at 1.8% year on year for August, level with July's reading and still short of the central bank's target. A steady print would extend a run of below-target core readings even as broader price pressure continues to build elsewhere in the economy. Producer prices, an upstream measure of the costs businesses eventually pass on to consumers, accelerated to their fastest pace in roughly three and a half years in August, adding to the case that inflation has further to run once government fuel subsidies are unwound.

None of this is likely to be the deciding input for the BoJ board, which wraps up a two-day meeting later today. A quarter point rate hike to 1.25% is close to fully priced by swap markets, and the case for tightening has already been built over recent months on a run of firm wage data, a weaker yen and warnings from board members including Hajime Takata that the bank should move nimbly if price pressure builds further. Today's CPI print will most likely be read as confirmation of the broader trend rather than a factor the board is waiting on before it acts.

The more market-moving event will be Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference this afternoon, where traders will parse his language for clues on the pace of further tightening beyond today's expected move. A hike would take Japan's policy rate to its highest level since 1993 and mark the BoJ's sixth increase since it exited ultra-loose policy in 2024. A separate, fuller preview of the rate decision will follow.

Le Japon doit publier aujourd'hui son indice national des prix à la consommation pour le mois d'août, un communiqué qui attirera moins l'attention que d'habitude étant donné que la décision politique de la Banque du Japon sera prise le même jour.Les chiffres de la région de Tokyo, considérés comme un indicateur avancé pour le nombre national, ont déjà donné aux commerçants une lecture précoce il y a trois semaines : l'IPC de base hors aliments frais a augmenté de 1,8% en glissement annuel en août, en légère hausse par rapport à 1,7% en juillet et en ligne avec la prévision médiane. Une jauge surveillée de près qui supprime à la fois les aliments frais et l'énergie a également légèrement augmenté, se rapprochant de l'objectif d'inflation de 2% de la BoJ.

Les économistes interrogés par Reuters s'attendent à ce que le chiffre national suive cette tendance, l'IPC de base devant se maintenir à 1,8% en glissement annuel en août, au même niveau que la lecture de juillet et toujours en deçà de l'objectif de la banque centrale. Une impression régulière prolongerait une série de lectures de base inférieures à la cible, même si une pression plus large sur les prix continue de s'accumuler ailleurs dans l'économie.Les prix à la production, une mesure en amont des coûts que les entreprises finissent par répercuter sur les consommateurs, ont accéléré à leur rythme le plus rapide en environ trois ans et demi en août, ajoutant au fait que l'inflation doit continuer à courir une fois que les subventions gouvernementales sur les carburants seront levées.

Rien de tout cela n'est susceptible d'être la contribution décisive pour le conseil d'administration de la BoJ, qui conclut une réunion de deux jours plus tard aujourd'hui. Une hausse des taux d'un quart de point à 1,25% est presque entièrement évaluée par les marchés des swaps, et les arguments en faveur d'un resserrement ont déjà été développés au cours des derniers mois sur la base de données salariales solides, d'un yen plus faible et des avertissements des membres du conseil d'administration, y compris Hajime Takata, selon lesquels la banque devrait se déplacer rapidement si la pression sur les prix s'intensifie.L'impression de l'IPC d'aujourd' hui sera très probablement lue comme une confirmation de la tendance plus large plutôt que comme un facteur que le conseil attend avant d'agir.

L'événement le plus dynamique du marché sera la conférence de presse du gouverneur Kazuo Ueda cet après-midi, où les traders analyseront son langage pour trouver des indices sur le rythme du resserrement au-delà du mouvement attendu aujourd'hui. Une hausse porterait le taux directeur du Japon à son plus haut niveau depuis 1993 et marquerait la sixième augmentation de la BoJ depuis sa sortie de la politique ultra-libre en 2024. Un aperçu séparé et plus complet de la décision tarifaire suivra.

cb_articles.contenu:
Before you bet on one-and-done consider the history

Welcome to the new rate-hike cycle.

The FOMC delivered on the market's expectation for a rate hike yesterday and moved the Fed funds range to 3.75-4.00% from 3.50-3.75%. A hawkish Q&A from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh left the market thinking there's an even chance of a second hike in October but there are still plenty of doves out there, who think inflation is transitory and will be quickly defeated. Part of the reason for that is that the starting point of this rate hiking cycle is relatively high and that the most rate-sensitive part of the economy -- housing -- is already in a multi-year slump.

Looking out the curve, the market sees three more hikes for a total of four and a terminal top of 4.50%-4.75%.

If you compare that to history, it would be an outlier. The smallest rate-hike cycle rise was in 1986-87 at 137 basis points in a move to 7.25% from 5.88%. That was followed by 1999-2000 at 1.75% and culminating at 6.50% Fed funds.

Deutsche Bank has a great chart showing the history of hiking cycles.

What's also worth focusing on here is the 'End' column because it's absolute, not relative. Even in the intense post-covid inflation regime, the top was 5.375% and that's the dove case for holding rates sooner. Even in that supply crunch, rates at 5.25-5.50% range did the job.

So the curve topping at 4.50%-4.75%. brings it close, another 3 hikes would be equally severe and right now, that kind of reaction seems unwarranted. Of course, that could change if we get an endless war and $200 oil.

What's more likely is that we start to get some US fiscal restraint in a divided Congress and the war ends. With that, I can get behind the market's thinking but be aware that history is not on the side of the curve.
cb_articles.contenu_fr:
Avant de parier sur le one-and-done, considérez l'historique

Bienvenue dans le nouveau cycle de hausse des tarifs.

Le FOMC a répondu aux attentes du marché en matière de hausse des taux hier et a fait passer la fourchette des fonds fédéraux de 3,50 à 3,75 % à 3,75 %. Une question-réponse belliciste du président de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, a quitté le marché en pensant qu'il y avait une chance égale d'une deuxième hausse en octobre, mais il y a encore beaucoup de colombes, qui pensent que l'inflation est transitoire et sera rapidement vaincue.Cela s'explique en partie par le fait que le point de départ de ce cycle de hausse des taux est relativement élevé et que la partie de l'économie la plus sensible aux taux - le logement - est déjà en récession pluriannuelle.

En regardant la courbe, le marché voit trois autres hausses pour un total de quatre et un sommet terminal de 4,50%-4,75%.

Si vous comparez cela à l'histoire, ce serait une valeur aberrante. La plus faible hausse du cycle de hausse des taux a eu lieu en 1986-1987 à 137 points de base, passant de 5,88 % à 7,25 %. Cela a été suivi par 1999-2000 à 1,75% et culminant à 6,50% des fonds fédéraux.

Deutsche Bank a un excellent tableau montrant l'histoire des cycles de randonnée.

Ce qui vaut également la peine de se concentrer ici, c'est la colonne « Fin », car elle est absolue et non relative. Même dans le régime d'inflation intense post-covid, le sommet était de 5,375% et c'est le cas de la colombe pour maintenir les taux plus tôt. Même dans cette crise d'approvisionnement, des taux compris entre 5,25 et 5,50 % ont fait l'affaire.

Donc, le sommet de la courbe à 4,50% -4,75% le rapproche, 3 autres hausses seraient tout aussi sévères et à l'heure actuelle, ce genre de réaction semble injustifié. Bien sûr, cela pourrait changer si nous obtenons une guerre sans fin et 200 $ de pétrole.

Ce qui est plus probable, c'est que nous commencions à obtenir des restrictions budgétaires américaines dans un Congrès divisé et que la guerre se termine. Avec cela, je peux prendre du retard sur la pensée du marché mais être conscient que l'histoire n'est pas du côté de la courbe.

cb_articles.contenu:
The BOE is widely expected to hold rates, but a 5-4 or 6-3 vote split could shape expectations heading into November

Barring a major surprise, there should not be too much suspense over the headline decision from the BOE later today. The central bank is widely expected to keep the bank rate at 3.75%, as markets are also pricing in nearly 80% odds of that outcome.

The more interesting question is what happens underneath that decision, and in particular whether the bank rate vote stays at 6-3 or narrows to 5-4.

The consensus is for another 6-3 vote, but the uncertainty centres mainly on which side of the fence Lombardelli decides to sit on. As things stand, she is the only wildcard after having previously highlighted the risk of second-round effects from persistently higher energy prices.

And energy prices have only moved higher since then, so the question is whether that has been enough to push her into the hawkish camp alongside Pill, Greene, and Mann.

While a 5-4 vote would not automatically tell us that a November rate hike is coming, but it would make the debate much more uncomfortable for the hold camp. That especially as markets are also preparing for it already, with the odds of a move in November priced at near 70% now.

Beyond the bank rate vote itself, I will be looking at whether any member describes the decision as being “finely balanced”. And also whether the collective guidance by the central bank becomes more explicit about the upside risks to inflation.

That will be measured against the current narrative of the central bank still weighing higher energy-driven inflation against the backdrop of a softer labour market and relatively limited evidence broader second-round effects, at least for now.

After the decision itself, Bailey and Lombardelli's individual paragraphs should probably be the first place to look. A 6-3 vote accompanied by largely unchanged language would suggest policymakers are still comfortable in waiting for more evidence before November. But on a 5-4 split, or stronger language about needing to act, would make the current November tightening expectations look better supported.

Besides the above, there is also the QT decision to watch. £50 billion is the clear consensus here for the annual APF rundown and some focus on whether the BOE reduces or ends long-dated gilt sales.

But for sterling and the front end of the gilt curve, the vote split and the message surrounding November should be doing most of the talking today.
cb_articles.contenu_fr:
On s'attend généralement à ce que la BOE maintienne les taux, mais une répartition des voix de 5-4 ou 6-3 pourrait façonner les attentes à l'approche de novembre

Sauf surprise majeure, il ne devrait pas y avoir trop de suspense sur la décision de la BOE plus tard dans la journée. On s'attend généralement à ce que la banque centrale maintienne le taux bancaire à 3,75 %, car les marchés évaluent également près de 80 % de chances de ce résultat.

La question la plus intéressante est de savoir ce qui se passe en vertu de cette décision, et en particulier si le vote sur le taux bancaire reste à 6-3 ou se réduit à 5-4.

Le consensus est pour un autre vote 6-3, mais l'incertitude est principalement de quel côté de la clôture Lombardelli décide de s'asseoir. En l'état actuel des choses, elle est le seul joker après avoir précédemment mis en évidence le risque d'effets de second tour de la hausse persistante des prix de l'énergie.

Et les prix de l'énergie n'ont fait que grimper depuis, donc la question est de savoir si cela a été suffisant pour la pousser dans le camp des faucons aux côtés de Pill, Greene et Mann.

Alors qu'un vote de 5-4 ne nous dirait pas automatiquement qu'une hausse des taux en novembre arrive, cela rendrait le débat beaucoup plus inconfortable pour le camp d'attente. Cela d'autant plus que les marchés s'y préparent déjà, avec les chances d'un déménagement en novembre à près de 70% maintenant.

Au-delà du vote sur le taux bancaire lui-même, je vérifierai si un membre décrit la décision comme étant « finement équilibrée ». Et aussi si les directives collectives de la banque centrale deviennent plus explicites sur les risques à la hausse pour l'inflation.

Cela sera mesuré par rapport au récit actuel selon lequel la banque centrale pèse toujours une inflation plus élevée tirée par l'énergie dans le contexte d'un marché du travail plus faible et d'effets de second tour relativement limités, du moins pour l'instant.

Après la décision elle-même, les paragraphes individuels de Bailey et Lombardelli devraient probablement être le premier endroit à regarder. Un vote 6-3 accompagné d'un libellé largement inchangé suggérerait que les décideurs politiques sont toujours à l'aise d'attendre plus de preuves avant novembre. Mais sur une division de 5-4, ou un langage plus fort sur la nécessité d'agir, les attentes actuelles de resserrement de novembre seraient mieux soutenues.

En plus de ce qui précède, il y a aussi la décision QT à surveiller. 50 milliards de £ est le consensus clair ici pour le récapitulatif annuel de l'APF et certains se concentrent sur la question de savoir si la BOE réduit ou met fin aux ventes de dorures à long terme.

Mais pour la livre sterling et l'extrémité avant de la courbe dorée, la division des votes et le message entourant novembre devraient faire la majeure partie de la conversation aujourd'hui.

cb_articles.contenu:
The Fed raised rates by 25 bps as expected yesterday and signalled another rate hike by year-end. How the did the outcome compare with the consensus?

The Fed raised rates by 25 bps as expected yesterday and signalled another rate hike by year-end. The market reaction was hawkish with stocks, bonds and gold falling and the US dollar rising. But was the outcome really that hawkish or the market just overreacted to nothing? Let's see how it compared to the prevailing market pricing, consensus and past commentary.

STATEMENT

The most notable changes in the statement were the vote split and the framing around inflation. The consensus was for one or two members dissenting in favour of a hold, but we got an unanimous decision. That could be read as slightly hawkish, but given the context and the credibility narrative, it's not such a big deal.

In July, the Fed said that inflation remained elevated, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy. Yesterday, they removed the supply shocks part. Again, it's not a big deal because many Fed members in the past weeks argued that the current persistence/breadth of inflation cannot be explained simply by the recent supply shocks.

Even Fed's Waller mentioned in July that core inflation had begun rising before the oil shock and recently he said elevated energy prices and tariffs were no longer a significant source of ongoing inflation pressure.

Image: July and September FOMC statement comparison (h/t newsquawk)

SUMMARY OF ECONOMIC PROJECTIONS AND DOT PLOT

The macroeconomic projections were mostly in line with the consensus, as we saw a downward revision to unemployment given the recent trend in the labour market and an upward revision to inflation due to the persistenly higher energy prices and AI driven demand. The Fed also slightly upgraded growth projections, but there wasn't a strong consensus on growth forecasts.

The focus was mainly on the dot plot, and this is where the Fed was less hawkish than expected. The consensus was for the Fed to signal one more rate hike in 2026 and one in 2027. The market, on the other hand, was pricing in one more in 2026 and two more in 2027.

The Fed met the 2026 consensus by projecting another rate hike, but missed entirely on 2027 where it just signalled rates to remain unchanged before rate cuts coming in 2028. The dot plot shows the committee bias and it clearly says that there isn't much willingness to tighten enough. They didn't even projected to erase the three rate cuts delivered in 2025.

Some said that the higher for longer stance in 2027 is hawkish. In reality, it doesn't matter that much because the Fed is going to change that into rate cuts as soon as oil prices tumble or we get soft economic data. What matters is their bias and it's not that hawkish.

PRESS CONFERENCE

The press conference is where I got surprised by people saying that Fed Chair Warsh was more hawkish than expected. In mypreview, I mentioned that the consensus was for Warsh to mostly repeat his Jackson Hole speech. That's exactly what he did.

You can compare his press conference remarks with the Jackson Hole speech and you will see that they are mostly the same. The only differences reflect the rate hike. For confirmation, you can ask ChatGPT to compare the speeches and it will tell you this:

"The second text (Jackson Hole) appears to be a substantial source/template for the first text (press conference remarks), with several phrases, arguments, sequencing choices, and data pointscarried over almost directly. The first text, however, reframes the material as a September 16 FOMC press conference following a 25 bp rate hike, whereas the second is a Jackson Hole speech focused on monetary-policy principles and the economy.

CONCLUSION

In summary, the Fed wasn't more hawkish than expected, I'd argue it was less hawkish. If you are looking at the markets and seeing everything erasing yesterday's moves, now you know why.The markets overreacted to nothingand are now going back to pre-FOMC levels.

Looking ahead, I would carefully watch the situation in the Middle East as $100 oil, rate hikes and elevated bond yields might put more pressure on Trump to end his war. Look for signs of de-escalation as that's going to weigh on oil prices. Oil has been the main driver of pretty much all other markets given its influence on inflation and interest rate expectations. Lower oil prices would trigger a dovish repricing and support risk sentiment. Of course the opposite is true if things escalate further.
cb_articles.contenu_fr:
La Fed a relevé ses taux de 25 points de base comme prévu hier et a signalé une nouvelle hausse des taux d'ici la fin de l'année. Comment le résultat se compare-t-il au consensus ?

La Fed a relevé ses taux de 25 points de base comme prévu hier et a signalé une nouvelle hausse des taux d'ici la fin de l'année. La réaction du marché a été belliciste avec la chute des actions, des obligations et de l'or et la hausse du dollar américain. Mais le résultat était-il vraiment que le faucon ou le marché avait simplement réagi de manière excessive à rien ? Voyons comment cela se compare aux prix du marché, au consensus et aux commentaires passés.

DÉCLARATION

Les changements les plus notables dans la déclaration ont été la répartition des voix et l'encadrement autour de l'inflation. Le consensus était pour un ou deux membres dissidents en faveur d'une suspension, mais nous avons obtenu une décision unanime. Cela pourrait être considéré comme un peu belliciste, mais compte tenu du contexte et du récit de crédibilité, ce n'est pas si grave.

En juillet, la Fed a déclaré que l'inflation restait élevée, en partie à cause des chocs d'offre qui ont entraîné des hausses de prix dans certains secteurs, y compris l'énergie. Hier, ils ont enlevé la partie des amortisseurs d'alimentation. Encore une fois, ce n'est pas un gros problème car de nombreux membres de la Fed au cours des dernières semaines ont fait valoir que la persistance/ampleur actuelle de l'inflation ne peut pas s'expliquer simplement par les récents chocs d'offre.

Même Waller de la Fed a mentionné en juillet que l'inflation de base avait commencé à augmenter avant le choc pétrolier et a récemment déclaré que les prix et les tarifs élevés de l'énergie n'étaient plus une source importante de pression inflationniste continue.

Image : Comparaison des relevés FOMC de juillet et septembre (h/t newsquawk)

RÉSUMÉ DES PROJECTIONS ÉCONOMIQUES ET GRAPHIQUE À POINTS

Les projections macroéconomiques étaient principalement conformes au consensus, car nous avons constaté une révision à la baisse du chômage compte tenu de la tendance récente du marché du travail et une révision à la hausse de l'inflation en raison de la hausse persistante des prix de l'énergie et de la demande liée à l'IA. La Fed a également légèrement revu à la hausse les projections de croissance, mais il n'y avait pas de consensus solide sur les prévisions de croissance.

L'accent était principalement mis sur l'intrigue à points, et c'est là que la Fed était moins belliciste que prévu. Le consensus était que la Fed devait signaler une nouvelle hausse des taux en 2026 et une autre en 2027. Le marché, en revanche, en fixait un de plus en 2026 et deux de plus en 2027.

La Fed a atteint le consensus de 2026 en prévoyant une nouvelle hausse des taux, mais a complètement raté 2027 où elle a simplement signalé que les taux resteraient inchangés avant les réductions de taux à venir en 2028. Le graphique à points montre le parti pris du comité et indique clairement qu'il n'y a pas beaucoup de volonté de resserrer suffisamment. Ils ne prévoyaient même pas d'effacer les trois réductions de taux livrées en 2025.

Certains ont dit que la position la plus élevée pour une position plus longue en 2027 est belliciste. En réalité, cela n'a pas beaucoup d'importance parce que la Fed va changer cela en baisses de taux dès que les prix du pétrole chuteront ou que nous obtiendrons des données économiques souples. Ce qui compte, c'est leur parti pris et ce n'est pas si belliciste que ça.

I - CONFERENCE DE PRESSE

La conférence de presse est l'endroit où j'ai été surpris par les gens qui disaient que le président de la Fed Warsh était plus belliciste que prévu. Dans mon entretien, j'ai mentionné que le consensus était que Warsh répétait principalement son discours de Jackson Hole. C'est exactement ce qu'il a fait.

Vous pouvez comparer ses remarques de conférence de presse avec le discours de Jackson Hole et vous verrez qu'elles sont pour la plupart les mêmes. Les seules différences reflètent la hausse des taux. Pour confirmation, vous pouvez demander à ChatGPT de comparer les discours et il vous dira ceci :

« Le deuxième texte (Jackson Hole) semble être une source/un modèle substantiel pour le premier texte (remarques de conférence de presse), avec plusieurs phrases, arguments, choix de séquençage et points de données reportés presque directement. Le premier texte, cependant, reformule le matériel comme une conférence de presse du FOMC du 16 septembre à la suite d'une hausse de taux de 25 pb, tandis que le second est un discours de Jackson Hole axé sur les principes de politique monétaire et l'économie.

CONCLUSION

En résumé, la Fed n'était pas plus belliciste que prévu, je dirais qu'elle était moins belliciste. Si vous regardez les marchés et que vous voyez tout effacer les mouvements d'hier, vous savez maintenant pourquoi. Les marchés ont réagi de manière excessive et reviennent maintenant aux niveaux pré-FOMC.

À l'avenir, je surveillerais attentivement la situation au Moyen-Orient, car le pétrole à 100 $ , les hausses de taux et les rendements obligataires élevés pourraient exercer plus de pression sur Trump pour qu'il mette fin à sa guerre. Recherchez des signes de désescalade car cela va peser sur les prix du pétrole. Le pétrole a été le principal moteur de presque tous les autres marchés compte tenu de son influence sur l'inflation et les anticipations de taux d'intérêt. La baisse des prix du pétrole déclencherait une réévaluation accommodante et soutiendrait le sentiment de risque.Bien sûr, le contraire est vrai si les choses dégénèrent davantage.

cb_articles.contenu:
Warsh’s first Fed rate hike sends a clear message that inflation credibility is the number one priority

There was always going to be more riding on this Fed decision than just another 25 bps rate hike.

For Kevin Warsh, this was also about establishing what his Fed is going to stand for - even this early on in his tenure as Fed chair.

The central bank finally decided to act after months of stubborn inflation, withincreasingly uncomfortable moves in the bond market arguably also backing policymakers into a corner.

The decision was ultimately unanimous in raising interest rates to 3.75% - 4.00%, but the more important aspect was everything around it.

In particular, the latestdot plotprojections show that 16 of 18 policymakers are expecting at least one more hike before year-end. That is not the kind of communique from a central bank that is merely looking to get this over and done with.

And Warsh also reinforced that message in his press conference, arguing that financial conditions were difficult to describe as being restrictive. In other words, the Fed does not think that one 25 bps move suddenly puts the brakes on the economy.

In keeping with his approach, he pushed back on the idea of forward guidance. While he did sound like he was ready to hike rates again, there was no firm pre-commitment on his part. Nonetheless, he came across as being more hawkish even if he still managed to play his political card right in not listing the US fiscal deficit as a key reason why bond yields have risen.

It was a difficult balance to strike, but Warsh managed to sound hawkish without putting the Fed on a predetermined rate path. And more importantly, he offered a credible answer to the questions surrounding the Fed's resolve on inflation without too much compromise.

That matters because credibility is not about sounding hawkish for the sake of it. It is more about convincing markets that when the Fed says inflation is unacceptable, policy will eventually follow those words.

US president Trump certainly wasn't happy with the decision, although his criticism still stopped short of turning directly on Warsh:

At this juncture, the Fed cannot keep insisting that price stability is paramount while treating persistent inflation as somebody else's problem. At some point, policy has to reflect that reality.

And yesterday's decision is one step in that direction at least.

For markets, they certainly got the message. The dollar strengthened, 2-year Treasury yields jumped and rate markets have moved to price roughly a 90% chance of another hike before year-end.

The reaction may not be to everyone's liking but it arguably beats the bond market from kicking and screaming if the Fed decided on a different decision path. But that is almost besides the point.

Warsh has repeatedly argued that the Fed needs to restore price stability. And after yesterday's decision, markets now have evidence that those words carry some weight.
cb_articles.contenu_fr:
La première hausse des taux de la Fed de Warsh envoie un message clair que la crédibilité de l'inflation est la priorité numéro un

Il y aura toujours plus de chevauchement sur cette décision de la Fed que juste une autre hausse de taux de 25 points de base.

Pour Kevin Warsh, il s'agissait également d'établir ce que sa Fed va défendre - même au début de son mandat de président de la Fed.

La banque centrale a finalement décidé d'agir après des mois d'inflation tenace, des mouvements de plus en plus inconfortables sur le marché obligataire qui ont sans doute également pris les décideurs dans un coin.

La décision a finalement été unanime pour relever les taux d'intérêt à 3,75 % - 4,00 %, mais l'aspect le plus important était tout ce qui l'entourait.

En particulier, les dernières projections de parcelles montrent que 16 des 18 décideurs politiques s'attendent à au moins une autre hausse avant la fin de l'année. Ce n'est pas le genre de communiqué d'une banque centrale qui cherche simplement à en finir.

Et Warsh a également renforcé ce message dans sa conférence de presse, faisant valoir que les conditions financières étaient difficiles à décrire comme étant restrictives. En d'autres termes, la Fed ne pense pas qu'un mouvement de 25 points de base mette soudainement un frein à l'économie.

Conformément à son approche, il a repoussé l'idée de guidage vers l'avant. Bien qu'il ait sonné comme s'il était prêt à relever à nouveau les taux, il n'y avait aucun pré-engagement ferme de sa part. Néanmoins, il a semblé être plus belliciste même s'il a quand même réussi à jouer sa carte politique en ne citant pas le déficit budgétaire américain comme l'une des principales raisons pour lesquelles les rendements obligataires ont augmenté.

C'était un équilibre difficile à trouver, mais Warsh a réussi à paraître belliciste sans mettre la Fed sur une trajectoire de taux prédéterminée. Et plus important encore, il a offert une réponse crédible aux questions entourant la résolution de la Fed sur l'inflation sans trop de compromis.

Cela compte parce que la crédibilité ne consiste pas à paraître belliciste pour le plaisir. Il s'agit plutôt de convaincre les marchés que lorsque la Fed dit que l'inflation est inacceptable, la politique suivra finalement ces mots.

Le président américain Trump n'était certainement pas satisfait de la décision, bien que ses critiques ne se soient toujours pas tournées directement vers Warsh :

À ce stade, la Fed ne peut pas continuer à insister sur le fait que la stabilité des prix est primordiale tout en traitant l'inflation persistante comme le problème de quelqu'un d'autre. À un moment donné, la politique doit refléter cette réalité.

Et la décision d'hier est au moins un pas dans cette direction.

Pour les marchés, ils ont certainement compris le message. Le dollar s'est renforcé, les rendements des bons du Trésor à 2 ans ont bondi et les marchés des taux ont évolué pour évaluer à environ 90 % les chances d'une autre hausse avant la fin de l'année.

La réaction peut ne pas plaire à tout le monde, mais elle bat sans doute le marché obligataire de donner des coups de pied et de crier si la Fed décidait d'un chemin de décision différent. Mais c'est presque hors sujet.

Warsh a soutenu à plusieurs reprises que la Fed doit rétablir la stabilité des prix. Et après la décision d'hier, les marchés ont maintenant la preuve que ces mots ont un certain poids.

TD Securities forecast ahead of the Fed's September meeting that the FOMC would deliver three hikes in this cycle: September's move plus two more in October and January 2027, reversing its prior on hold call after hot August CPI data.

Because this call predates the meeting, its real market relevance now lies in whether it survives contact with what the Fed actually signalled. TD's January leg sits ahead of the Fed's own median dot, which points to only one further hike this year rather than two, so the call is currently more hawkish than the central bank's own guidance rather than confirming it.

If TD reaffirms the sequencing in the coming days, that would put it in a small group withGoldman Sachspushing timelines earlier than the December consensus most other major banks still hold, reinforcing the case for near term dollar strength and pressure on rate sensitive assets. If TD instead walks back the January leg once the dot plot's actual message is fully digested, that would suggest the initial post CPI shift was more about the inflation print than a considered read of the Fed's own reaction function.

TD called three Fed hikes before the Fed had even delivered its first one, and now that call has to hold up against the central bank's own dot plot.

TD Securities forecast ahead of the Fed's meeting yesterday a total of three hikes in this cycle: September, October and January 2027

The call reversed TD's prior expectation that the Fed would hold rates steady through the rest of 2026

The shift followed a hotter than expected August CPI report released the same week

Strategists Oscar Munoz and Gennadiy Goldberg said they expected no explicit forward guidance from the Fed but a hawkish dot plot

The September hike hassince been deliveredas expected, taking the fed funds range to 3.75% to 4.00%

The Fed's own dot plot pointed to only one additional 2026 hike, putting TD's January leg ahead of the central bank's median guidance; whether TD has updated the call since Wednesday's meeting is not yet clear

TD Securities forecast on September 11, five days ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting, that the central bank would deliver a total of three interest rate hikes in this cycle, reversing its previous call that the Fed would remain on hold for the rest of 2026. Strategists Oscar Munoz and Gennadiy Goldberg wrote that they expected the first hike to land at the September meeting, with the next two increases following in October and January 2027.

The revision came in direct response to the August consumer price index report released the same week, which came in hotter than expected and raised fresh doubts that inflation was making sufficient progress toward the Fed's target. TD's strategists said the data showed inflation had not cooled fast enough, and while they expected the Fed to withhold explicit forward guidance at the September meeting, they anticipated the accompanying dot plot would still lean hawkish.

The call placed TD among a wider group of major banks that abandoned earlier expectations for the Fed to hold rates steady through the remainder of 2026 after the same CPI report, though TD's specific timeline, three hikes concluding in January 2027 rather than the more common two hike, December endpoint forecast at the time, made it one of the more aggressive calls on the street heading into the meeting. The September hike itself has since been delivered as TD and most of the market expected, taking the fed funds range to 3.75% to 4.00%. What remains to be tested is the second half of TD's call, the specific timing of October and January moves, against a Fed dot plot that pointed to only one additional hike this year rather than two, a detail that puts TD's January leg of the forecast somewhat ahead of the central bank's own median guidance.

Whether TD has revisited or reaffirmed that October and January sequencing since Wednesday's meeting and dot plot release is not yet clear from available reporting, and any update the desk publishes in the coming days would be the new update, and would be the more immediate test of whether this call holds up against the Fed's own signalling.

Valeurs Mobilières TD prévoit, avant la réunion de septembre de la Fed, que le FOMC effectuerait trois hausses au cours de ce cycle : le déménagement de septembre et deux autres en octobre et janvier 2027, inversant sa précédente mise en attente après les données chaudes d'août sur l'IPC.

Parce que cet appel est antérieur à la réunion, sa véritable pertinence sur le marché réside maintenant dans sa capacité à survivre au contact avec ce que la Fed a réellement signalé. L'étape de janvier de la TD se situe devant le point médian de la Fed, qui ne signale qu'une seule hausse supplémentaire cette année plutôt que deux, de sorte que l'appel est actuellement plus belliciste que les propres directives de la banque centrale plutôt que de le confirmer.

Si la TD réaffirme le séquençage dans les prochains jours, cela le placerait dans un petit groupe avec des échéanciers Goldman Sachspushing plus tôt que le consensus de décembre que la plupart des autres grandes banques détiennent encore, renforçant ainsi les arguments en faveur de la vigueur du dollar à court terme et de la pression sur les actifs sensibles aux taux.Si la TD revient plutôt sur l'étape de janvier une fois que le message réel du graphique à points est entièrement digéré, cela suggérerait que le décalage initial après l'IPC concernait davantage l'impression de l'inflation qu'une lecture réfléchie de la propre fonction de réaction de la Fed.

La TD a appelé trois hausses de la Fed avant même que la Fed n'en ait livré une première, et maintenant cet appel doit résister à la propre intrigue à points de la banque centrale.

Valeurs Mobilières TD prévoit avant la réunion de la Fed d'hier un total de trois hausses dans ce cycle : septembre, octobre et janvier 2027

L'appel a inversé l'attente antérieure de la TD selon laquelle la Fed maintiendrait les taux stables jusqu'à la fin de 2026

Le changement a fait suite à un rapport sur l'IPC d'août plus chaud que prévu publié la même semaine

Les stratèges Oscar Munoz et Gennadiy Goldberg ont déclaré qu'ils ne s'attendaient à aucune orientation explicite de la part de la Fed, mais à un complot à points belliciste

La hausse de septembre a depuis été livrée comme prévu, portant la fourchette des fonds fédéraux à 3,75 % à 4,00 %

Le propre graphique à points de la Fed n'indiquait qu'une seule hausse supplémentaire en 2026, plaçant la jambe de janvier de la TD en avance sur les prévisions médianes de la banque centrale ; il n'est pas encore clair si la TD a mis à jour l'appel depuis la réunion de mercredi

Valeurs Mobilières TD a prévu le 11 septembre, cinq jours avant la réunion de la Réserve fédérale, que la banque centrale effectuerait un total de trois hausses de taux d'intérêt au cours de ce cycle, annulant son précédent appel selon lequel la Fed resterait en attente pour le reste de 2026. Les stratèges Oscar Munoz et Gennadiy Goldberg ont écrit qu'ils s'attendaient à ce que la première randonnée atterrisse lors de la réunion de septembre, les deux prochaines augmentations ayant lieu en octobre et janvier 2027.

La révision est intervenue en réponse directe au rapport sur l'indice des prix à la consommation publié en août la même semaine, qui a été plus chaud que prévu et a soulevé de nouveaux doutes sur le fait que l'inflation progressait suffisamment vers l'objectif de la Fed.Les stratèges de la TD ont déclaré que les données montraient que l'inflation ne s'était pas refroidie assez rapidement et, bien qu'ils s'attendaient à ce que la Fed refuse de donner des indications explicites sur les perspectives lors de la réunion de septembre, ils prévoyaient que le graphique à points qui l'accompagnait serait toujours très tendu.

L'appel a placé la TD parmi un groupe plus large de grandes banques qui ont abandonné les attentes antérieures de la Fed de maintenir les taux stables jusqu'à la fin de 2026 après le même rapport sur l'IPC, bien que le calendrier spécifique de la TD, trois hausses se terminant en janvier 2027 plutôt que les deux hausses plus courantes, le point final prévu en décembre à l'époque, en ait fait l'un des appels les plus agressifs de la rue avant la réunion.La hausse de septembre elle-même a depuis été livrée comme prévu par la TD et la majeure partie du marché, portant la fourchette des fonds fédéraux à 3,75 % à 4,00 %. Ce qui reste à tester, c'est la deuxième moitié de l'appel de la TD, le calendrier précis des mouvements d'octobre et de janvier, par rapport à un graphique de la Fed dot qui indiquait seulement une hausse supplémentaire cette année plutôt que deux, un détail qui place l'étape de janvier des prévisions de la TD un peu en avance sur les propres prévisions médianes de la banque centrale.

Si la TD a revisité ou réaffirmé que le séquençage d'octobre et de janvier depuis la réunion de mercredi et la publication de l'intrigue à points n'est pas encore clair à partir des rapports disponibles, et toute mise à jour publiée par le bureau dans les prochains jours serait la nouvelle mise à jour, et serait le test le plus immédiat pour savoir si cet appel résiste à la propre signalisation de la Fed.

Goldman Sachs has abandoned its one and done call and now expects a second 25bp Fed hike in October, saying Wednesday's meeting was more hawkish than expected on the dot plot, the elevated neutral rate estimate and Warsh's own comments.

Goldman moving to October rather than December for the next hike tightens the near term calendar markets have to price around, and puts a live meeting risk squarely inside a window some had assumed the Fed would prefer to avoid given its closeness to the midterms. If other desks follow Goldman in pulling their own timelines forward, that would likely keep short end yields and the dollar supported into October, while adding to the case for a higher for longer rate path more broadly. The bigger shift here is arguably qualitative rather than quantitative: with Goldman abandoning the most dovish framing on the street, the range of outcomes priced into rates markets narrows toward the more hawkish end, which typically weighs on rate sensitive equity valuations and can pressure risk assets that had been leaning on a shallower tightening path.

---Goldman just gave up on "one and done," and now it's the bank penciling in the soonest next move on the Fed's calendar.

Goldman Sachs now expects a second 25bp Fed hike in October, dropping its prior call that September's hike would be the only one this year

The shift puts Goldman ahead of JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley, both of which have been forecasting December for the next move

Goldman flagged three reasons Wednesday's meeting wasmore hawkish than expected: a 16 to 2 dot plot majority for at least one more 2026 hike with no dissents on the actual vote, an elevated median rate path through 2029, and a neutral rate estimate raised to 3.25% from 3.06%

Chair Kevin Warsh's repeated framing of the hike as removing policy accommodation was read by Goldman as building the case for further tightening

The revision narrows the gap between Goldman and the more hawkish banks, and raises the odds of a live October meeting some had assumed would be skipped due to its proximity to the midterms

Goldman Sachs has scrapped its one and done call on the Federal Reserve and now expects the FOMC to deliver a second 25 basis point rate hike in October, a reversal from its prior view that Wednesday's move would be the only increase this year. The shift marks one of the more notable changes in Wall Street's post meeting positioning, since it puts Goldman's timeline ahead of both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley, which have been pointing to December for a follow up move rather than October.

Goldman's economists said Wednesday's meeting came across as more hawkish than they had anticipated in three distinct respects.

First, a 16 to 2 majority of FOMC participants projected at least one more hike this year in the updated dot plot, and the actual rate decision itself carried no dissenting votes at all.

Second, the median funds rate projection stayed notably elevated all the way through 2029, while the median estimate of the neutral rate, the level policymakers see as neither stimulative nor restrictive, rose to 3.25% from 3.06% in the prior projections.

Third, Chair Kevin Warsh repeatedly characterized the hike during his remarks as having removed a degree of policy accommodation, a framing Goldman's team read as him actively building the case for further tightening rather than presenting Wednesday's move as a standalone, defensive step.

Taken together, those three signals appear to have done more to shift Goldman's outlook than the headline rate decision itself, which had been fully priced in and matched the bank's own forecast going into the meeting. The change brings Goldman's near term rate path closer in line with the Fed's own median guidance, and narrows the gap that had opened up between Goldman's more dovish framing and the more hawkish calls already in place at rival banks. It also raises the prospect of a live October meeting, a timing some commentators had previously flagged as unlikely given its proximity to the November midterm elections, though Goldman's revised call suggests that consideration may carry less weight with the committee than had been assumed.
cb_articles.contenu_fr:
Goldman Sachs a abandonné son appel unique et s'attend maintenant à une deuxième hausse de 25 pb de la Fed en octobre, affirmant que la réunion de mercredi était plus belliciste que prévu sur le graphique à points, l'estimation du taux neutre élevé et les propres commentaires de Warsh.

Le passage de Goldman en octobre plutôt qu'en décembre pour la prochaine hausse resserre les marchés du calendrier à court terme et place un risque de réunion en direct carrément à l'intérieur d'une fenêtre que certains avaient supposé que la Fed préférerait éviter étant donné sa proximité avec les midterms.Si d'autres bureaux suivent Goldman en tirant leurs propres calendriers vers l'avant, cela maintiendrait probablement les rendements à court terme et le dollar soutenu jusqu'en octobre, tout en ajoutant à l'argument en faveur d'un chemin de taux plus élevé pour plus long plus largement.Le changement le plus important ici est sans doute qualitatif plutôt que quantitatif : Goldman abandonnant le cadrage le plus dovish de la rue, la gamme de résultats évalués sur les marchés des taux se rétrécit vers l'extrémité plus belliciste, ce qui pèse généralement sur les valorisations des actions sensibles aux taux et peut exercer une pression sur les actifs à risque qui s'appuyaient sur un resserrement moins profond.

---Goldman vient d'abandonner sur « un et fait », et maintenant c'est la banque qui crayonne dans le prochain mouvement le plus tôt sur le calendrier de la Fed.

Goldman Sachs s'attend maintenant à une deuxième hausse de 25 pb de la Fed en octobre, abandonnant son appel précédent selon lequel la hausse de septembre serait la seule cette année

Le changement place Goldman devant JPMorgan et Morgan Stanley, qui ont tous deux prévu décembre pour la prochaine étape

Goldman a signalé trois raisons pour lesquelles la réunion de mercredi était plus belliciste que prévu : une majorité de 16 à 2 points pour au moins une autre hausse de 2026 sans aucune dissidence sur le vote réel, une trajectoire de taux médian élevée jusqu'en 2029 et une estimation de taux neutre portée à 3,25 % contre 3,06 %

La formulation répétée de la randonnée par le président Kevin Warsh, à savoir la suppression des accommodements politiques, a été lue par Goldman comme plaidant en faveur d'un resserrement supplémentaire

La révision réduit l'écart entre Goldman et les banques plus bellicistes, et augmente les chances d'une réunion en direct en octobre que certains avaient supposée être ignorée en raison de sa proximité avec les midterms

Goldman Sachs a abandonné son appel à la Réserve fédérale et s'attend maintenant à ce que le FOMC procède à une deuxième hausse de taux de 25 points de base en octobre, un renversement par rapport à son point de vue précédent selon lequel la décision de mercredi serait la seule augmentation cette année.Ce changement marque l'un des changements les plus notables dans le positionnement de Wall Street après les réunions, car il place le calendrier de Goldman devant JPMorgan et Morgan Stanley, qui ont indiqué décembre pour un suivi plutôt qu'octobre.

Les économistes de Goldman ont déclaré que la réunion de mercredi était plus belliciste qu'ils ne l'avaient prévu à trois égards distincts.

Tout d'abord, une majorité de 16 à 2 participants au FOMC a projeté au moins une hausse supplémentaire cette année dans le graphique à points mis à jour, et la décision de taux elle-même n'a recueilli aucun vote dissident.

Deuxièmement, la projection du taux médian des fonds est restée considérablement élevée tout au long de 2029, tandis que l'estimation médiane du taux neutre, le niveau que les décideurs considèrent comme ni stimulant ni restrictif, est passée de 3,06 % à 3,25 % dans les projections précédentes.

Troisièmement, le président Kevin Warsh a caractérisé à plusieurs reprises la randonnée au cours de ses remarques comme ayant supprimé un certain degré d'accommodement politique, une équipe de Goldman a lu qu'il construisait activement les arguments en faveur d'un resserrement supplémentaire plutôt que de présenter la décision de mercredi comme une étape autonome et défensive.

Pris ensemble, ces trois signaux semblent avoir fait plus pour changer les perspectives de Goldman que la décision de taux global elle-même, qui avait été entièrement évaluée et correspondait aux propres prévisions de la banque avant la réunion.Le changement rapproche la trajectoire des taux à court terme de Goldman des prévisions médianes de la Fed et réduit l'écart qui s'était ouvert entre le cadre plus conciliant de Goldman et les appels plus bellicistes déjà en place dans les banques rivales.Cela soulève également la perspective d'une réunion en direct en octobre, un moment que certains commentateurs avaient précédemment signalé comme improbable compte tenu de sa proximité avec les élections de mi-mandat de novembre, bien que l'appel révisé de Goldman suggère que la considération pourrait avoir moins de poids avec le comité que ce qui avait été supposé.

The IMF says the RBA should stand ready to hike further on energy driven inflation risk, downgrading Australia's 2027 growth forecast to 1.6% and urging governments to cut spending, with markets pricing an 80% chance of a hike on September 29.

The IMF's warning adds institutional weight to what markets are already pricing, anRBA hike as soon as September 29,and reinforces AUD support at the margin given the fund is flagging upside inflation risk rather than downside growth risk as the dominant concern. The bigger swing factor for the Aussie near term is energy prices rather than the IMF statement itself, given Brent's 35% surge since early August on the worsening Middle East conflict is the direct channel the IMF says could force the RBA's hand through second round inflation effects. With the Fed also having just hiked, a hawkish RBA move would keep Australia in step with a broader global tightening pulse, which should be a supportive combination for AUD crosses funded in currencies where central banks are seen as closer to done.

---The IMF is telling Australia to tighten the budget and stay ready to tighten rates further, with surging fuel prices doing much of the work behind that warning.

IMF says the RBA should stand ready to hike rates further given persistent underlying inflation and uncertainty over how restrictive policy currently is

IMF forecasts Australian GDP growth of 1.9% this year, cut to 1.6% in 2027, a downgrade it attributes to the higher chance of another RBA hike

Key risk flagged: further spikes in global energy prices could trigger second round inflation effects requiring more tightening

Brent crude surged 35% since early August to above $108 a barrel on Wednesday on worsening Middle East conflict; Australian core and headline CPI already topped forecasts in July

Markets are pricing around an 80% chance of a 25bp RBA hike at its September 29 meeting, with some estimates as high as 87% and the cash rate reaching 4.85% by early 2027

IMF also urged federal and state governments to cut spending, while largely backing Labor's investor tax changes; mission chief Paulo Medas said the changes create more balanced incentives that could help housing affordability

The International Monetary Fund said on Thursday that Australia's central bank may need to raise interest rates further, warning that persistent underlying inflation pressures and uncertainty over whether financial conditions are sufficiently restrictive mean the Reserve Bank of Australia should stand ready to hike as needed. The warning came in the IMF's concluding statement following its annual consultations with Treasury, the RBA and the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority.

The fund downgraded its forecast for Australian economic growth, predicting the economy will expand 1.9% this year before slowing to 1.6% in 2027, a 0.1 percentage point cut from its previous projection. It attributed the downgrade to the higher likelihood of another RBA rate increase. Inflation remains a central challenge, the IMF said, while weak productivity growth is weighing on the economy's potential. The fund flagged a specific risk that further large increases in global energy prices could produce stronger second round effects, lifting inflation expectations and warranting additional tightening from the RBA, which targets inflation between 2% and 3%.

That risk is not hypothetical. Fuel prices in Australia are rising again after the worsening Middle East conflict pushed Brent crude above 108 US dollars a barrel on Wednesday, a 35% surge since the start of August. Australian consumer prices already rose more than expected in July as fuel costs jumped, with core inflation also topping forecasts. Financial markets are pricing around an 80% chance the RBA raises its 4.35% cash rate by 25 basis points at its September 29 meeting, with some estimates putting the probability as high as 87% and seeing the cash rate reach 4.85% by early 2027. The Federal Reserve's own rate increase on Wednesday night, its first since 2023, adds to the global backdrop of tightening the RBA is weighing against.

Alongside its rate warning, the IMF urged Australia's federal and state governments to cut spending, arguing more disciplined budgets would help rein in rising debt burdens and support the fight against inflation. The assessment lands as a setback for treasurer Jim Chalmers, who is already under pressure to present a convincing story on living standards and prosperity. The fund did, however, largely back the government's changes to investor tax settings, while flagging some concerns about unintended consequences. IMF mission chief Paulo Medas said earlier consultations had identified Australia's property tax settings, including negative gearing, as creating incentives for households to take on more leverage and invest in housing, adding to price pressures. He said the government's budget changes had produced a more balanced set of incentives that could direct more investment toward other parts of the economy, calling it a positive change to the tax system that could help with housing affordability.

More than one hike before year end is not out of the question with sticky high inflaiton.
